annotation.title_clean: Too familiar to ignore, but too different to tolerate: The role of the law in regulating emotional expression by robots to mitigate the harmful effects of robot deception
annotation.title_en: Too familiar to ignore, but too different to tolerate: The role of the law in regulating emotional expression by robots to mitigate the harmful effects of robot deception
annotation.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Research Symposium 2025, University of Colombo
annotation.summary_en: Conference abstract analysing how law should regulate emotional expression by robots to mitigate harms of robot deception. Combines conceptual analysis with doctrinal review of the EU AI Act, finding harm from expressive robots underestimated, and proposes broader harm definitions, classification by deceptive capability, and design limits keeping robots in the uncanny valley.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robot deception through emotional expression is a distinct ethical and regulatory challenge
The EU AI Act underestimates harm from expressive robots
Expand the definition of harm to include long-term structural harm
Classify robots by their differing deceptive capabilities
Consider design restrictions that trap expressive robots in the uncanny valley
